literature.label: Erdős 1948: the full Lambert series is irrational
literature.statement: Erdős proved that the full series $X_{\mathbb{N}_{>0}}(b)$ is irrational at every integer base [erdos1948].

literature.label: Erdős 1968: pairwise coprime supports of finite reciprocal sum
literature.statement: Erdős later obtained the same conclusion for pairwise coprime supports of finite reciprocal sum [erdos1968, p. 222]. On that page he remarked that the coprimality assumption could be removed, and gave no details.

literature.label: Tao and Teräväinen 2025: the prime support at base two
literature.statement: Tao and Teräväinen nevertheless prove that $X_{\mathcal P}(2)$ is irrational [taoteravainen2025, Theorem 1.3, p. 4].

literature.label: Duverney and Tachiya: squarefree and s-free products
literature.locator: Forum Math. 31 (2019), Corollary 1.2 and Example 1.1, p. 4 of the author preprint
literature.statement: For squarefree support, irrationality already follows from the theorem of Duverney and Tachiya, at every base $2^j$ with $j\ge1$, by their Corollary 1.2 and Example 1.1 [duverneytachiya, p. 4]. Their corollary covers the $s$-free products of any pairwise coprime sequence of polynomial growth.

literature.label: Erdős 1975: a growth criterion
literature.statement: If $A=\{c_1<c_2<\cdots\}$ and $\limsup_n c_n/2^n=\infty$, then $X_A(b)$ is irrational for every integer $b\ge2$ [erdos1975, Theorem 1].

steps.label: The displacement identity (D)
steps.statement: For a positive integer $N$, $\Delta_{b,A}(N)=\sum_{a\in A}\frac{b^{N\bmod a}-1}{b^a-1}=(b^N-1)X_A(b)-J_{b,A}(N)$ with $J_{b,A}(N)=\sum_{a\in A,\,a\le N}\sum_{j=1}^{\lfloor N/a\rfloor}b^{N-ja}$. The identity follows on dividing $N$ by each $a$. At an integer base $J_{b,A}(N)$ is an integer.

steps.label: The displacement is positive for infinite support
steps.statement: For infinite $A$ the displacement $\Delta_{b,A}(N)$ is positive, because some $a\in A$ exceeds $N$.

uses.warrant: The positivity is stated for the displacement defined in (D): "for infinite $A$ the displacement $\Delta_{b,A}(N)$ is positive, because some $a\in A$ exceeds $N$".

steps.label: Rationality forces displacements of at least 1/q
steps.statement: If $X_A(b)=p/q$ with $p\in\mathbb Z$ and $q\ge1$ an integer, then $q\Delta_{b,A}(N)$ is a positive integer and $\Delta_{b,A}(N)\ge1/q$. It therefore suffices to find displacements tending to zero.

uses.warrant: The paper derives the bound from (D): "At an integer base $J_{b,A}(N)$ is an integer", so $q\Delta_{b,A}(N)$ is an integer.
The same paragraph uses positivity: "Hence, if $X_A(b)=p/q$ ... then $q\Delta_{b,A}(N)$ is a positive integer".

steps.label: The one-exponent orbit bound (2)
steps.statement: Put $d_a(m)=(b^{m\bmod a}-1)/(b^a-1)$ and $g=(Q,a)$. Then $\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T d_a(tQ)\le \frac{g}{a(b^g-1)}+\frac1{T(b^g-1)}$.

steps.label: The outer bound (3)
steps.statement: For $Y=QT$, $\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{a\in A,\,a>Y}d_a(tQ)\le\frac4T$, because $d_a(tQ)\le2\,2^{tQ-a}$ when $a>QT$ and $\sum_{t=1}^T2^{tQ-QT}\le2$.

steps.label: The dyadic estimate (4)
steps.statement: For integers $Q,M\ge1$ and $\alpha_a\ge0$ with $\sum_a\alpha_a/a<\infty$, $\sum_{j=M}^{2M-1}\frac1{2^j}\sum_{a\le Q2^j}\alpha_a\le2Q\sum_{a\ge1}\frac{\alpha_a}{a}$; the estimate remains valid if the dyadic lengths start later.

steps.label: The choice of modulus
steps.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.2, 'Choosing the modulus', p. 4
steps.statement: With $p_*=\max P$ and $H\ge2p_*$, set $Q=L\prod_{p\in P}p^{\lfloor\log_pH\rfloor}$ and $G=\lfloor H/p_*\rfloor$. For $a\notin F$ with $h(a)\le H$ we have $h(a)\mid Q$, hence $(Q,a)\ge h(a)$; for $h(a)>H$ we have $(Q,a)\ge G$ instead.

uses.warrant: The paper applies the choice to the complete-period term: "the complete-period term in (2) is at most $h(a)/[a(b^{h(a)}-1)]$".

steps.label: The combined bound (5)
steps.statement: $\frac1M\sum_{j=M}^{2M-1}\frac1{2^j}\sum_{t=1}^{2^j}\Delta_{b,A}(tQ)\le \varepsilon+\frac{2QW_{b,P}(A)}M+\frac{G(1+\log Q+2M\log2)+Q}{b^G-1}+4\,2^{-M}$, and with $F$ and $L$ fixed every term after $\varepsilon$ tends to zero as $H\to\infty$.

uses.warrant: "We apply (4) with $\alpha_a={\bf1}_A(a)/(b^{h(a)}-1)$" in the paragraph leading to (5).
"Together with (3), the preceding estimates give" (5); the last term accounts for the tail $a>QT$.
The terms of (5) are the costs computed for $h(a)\le H$ and $h(a)>H$ under the chosen $Q$ and $G$, with $M=\lfloor b^{G/2}\rfloor$.
"The first two terms account for the complete and incomplete periods of exponents with $h(a)\le H$", which (2) bounds.

steps.label: Weighted sums decrease with the base and on subsets
steps.locator: End of the proof of Theorem 1.2, p. 5
steps.statement: Finally, $W_{b,P}(A)\le W_{2,P}(A)$ for $b\ge2$, and the weighted sum can only decrease when we pass to a subset.

steps.label: The incidence form (6)
steps.statement: $c_A(n)=\#\{a\in A:a\mid n\}$ and $X_A(b)=\sum_{n\ge1}c_A(n)b^{-n}$. This follows on expanding $(b^a-1)^{-1}=\sum_{j\ge1}b^{-aj}$ and interchanging the nonnegative sums.

steps.label: Divisor majorants and the cover condition (V)
steps.statement: For each $j\ge1$, $F_j\subseteq\mathbb{N}_{>0}$ is finite, $0<\alpha_j\le1$, and $c_{j,d}\ge0$ satisfy $f_{F_j}(n)^{\alpha_j}\le\sum_{d\mid n}c_{j,d}$ $(n\ge1)$. With $C_j=\sum_{d\ge1}c_{j,d}/d$, condition (V) is $\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{C_j2^{j\alpha_j}}{2^{\alpha_j}-1}<\infty$.

steps.label: The finite kernel estimate (S)
steps.locator: Section 3, 'A finite mean for shifted divisor tails', estimate (S)
steps.statement: For $1<B\le2$, positive integers $L,d,M$ and an integer $R\ge0$, with $w_{B,d}(n)=B^{n\bmod d}/(B^d-1)$: $\mathscr D_{L;R,M}w_{B,d}\le\frac{1+4L/M}{d(B-1)}$.

steps.label: Subadditivity links the tails U_j and V_j
steps.statement: With $B_j=2^{\alpha_j}$, $U_j(N)=\sum_{r\ge1}2^{-r}f_{F_j}(N+r)$ and $V_j(N)=\sum_{d\ge1}c_{j,d}w_{B_j,d}(N)$: $U_j(N)^{\alpha_j}\le\sum_{r\ge1}B_j^{-r}f_{F_j}(N+r)^{\alpha_j}\le\sum_{d\ge1}c_{j,d}\sum_{r\ge1,\,d\mid N+r}B_j^{-r}=V_j(N)$.

uses.warrant: "Subadditivity of $x\mapsto x^{\alpha_j}$ and the divisor majorant connect the two"; the majorant is the hypothesis $f_{F_j}(n)^{\alpha_j}\le\sum_{d\mid n}c_{j,d}$.

steps.label: The cover displacement is at most the tail U_j
steps.statement: For the displacement itself, the geometric-series identity gives $\Delta_{2,F_j}(N)=U_j(N)-X_{F_j}(2)\le U_j(N)$.

steps.label: The base comparison Δ_b ≤ Δ_2
steps.locator: End of the proof of Theorem 3.1
steps.statement: For $0\le r<d$ the function $(b^r-1)/(b^d-1)$ is nonincreasing on $b>1$. Hence $\Delta_{b,A}(N)\le\Delta_{2,A}(N)$ for every real $b\ge2$.

steps.label: One index controls every cover tail
steps.statement: With allowances $t_j=\varepsilon2^{-j}$, choose $J$ with $K_J=\sum_{j>J}C_jt_j^{-\alpha_j}/(B_j-1)<1/4$ and $L$ divisible by every member of the first $J$ finite sets. For $M\ge4L$, (S) bounds the $\mathscr D_{L;R,M}$-mean of $S_J(N)=\sum_{j>J}t_j^{-\alpha_j}V_j(N)$ by $(1+4L/M)K_J<1/2$, so some sample satisfies $S_J(N)<1$, hence $U_j(N)<t_j$ for every $j>J$ and $0<\Delta_{2,A}(N)\le\sum_{j>J}U_j(N)\le\varepsilon$.

uses.warrant: "the estimate (S) bounds the $\mathscr D_{L;R,M}$-mean of $S_J(N)$ by $(1+4L/M)K_J<1/2$".
"Since $t_j^{-\alpha_j}V_j<1$ implies $U_j<t_j$", using $U_j^{\alpha_j}\le V_j$.
The final display $0<\Delta_{2,A}(N)\le\sum_{j>J}U_j(N)\le\varepsilon$ bounds the displacement by the tails.
Choosing $J$ with $K_J<1/4$ "is possible because $\varepsilon^{-\alpha_j}\le\max(1,\varepsilon^{-1})$" and (V) is summable.

steps.label: One distribution for both errors
steps.statement: Both estimates use $\mathscr D_{Q;M,M}$ with $Q=L\prod_{p\in P}p^{\lfloor\log_pH\rfloor}$, $G=\lfloor H/\max P\rfloor$, $M=\lfloor2^{G/2}\rfloor$. Then $\mathscr D_{Q;M,M}(\Delta_{2,E}/\rho)<\frac18$ and $\mathscr D_{Q;M,M}S_J\le(1+4Q/M)K_J<\frac18$, so $\mathscr D_{Q;M,M}(\Delta_{2,E}/\rho+S_J)<\frac14$. This step uses only the linearity of the mean, and requires no independence between the two errors.

uses.warrant: "The estimate (5) allows any common multiple of $F$ as $L$, so it accommodates the extra divisors required by the cover."
"On the same finite distribution, (S) and the interchange of nonnegative sums give" the bound on $S_J$.
"$U_j^{\alpha_j}\le V_j$ gives $U_j(N)<t_j$ for every $j>J$" at the chosen index.
The proof uses "the cover notation $B_j,U_j,V_j$ above" and chooses $J$ with $K_J<1/16$ from the summable cover cost.

steps.label: The logarithmic obstruction (7)
steps.statement: For every finite $F\subseteq\bigcup_jF_j$, $K\ge\mathbb E_F\Psi(f_F)\ge e\,\mathbb E_F\log^+f_F$, where $K=\sum_jC_j\eta_j^{-\alpha_j}/(2^{\alpha_j}-1)$ and $\Psi(t)=\inf_{0<\alpha\le1}t^\alpha/(2^\alpha-1)$.

steps.label: A weighted support with no divisor cover
steps.statement: With pairwise disjoint finite sets $P_k$ of odd primes such that $2^k/4\le S_k<2^k/4+1$ and $E=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\{2^kd:d\mid M_k\}$, the weighted sum for $P=\{2\}$ is finite, while $\mathbb E_{F_m}\log^+f_{F_m}\ge\frac{m-1}{8}\log2$. Thus $E\notin\mathcal C$.

uses.warrant: "By (7), a cover satisfying (V) would bound all these means by its fixed cost, which is impossible since they grow with $m$."

steps.label: A divisor cover with no finite-prime weighted condition
steps.statement: With odd primes $q_j\ge4^j$, disjoint prime sets $P_j$ and $V=\bigcup_{j\ge1}F_j$, $F_j=\{q_jd:d\mid M_j\}$: $\sum_{a\in V}1/a$ diverges, $V\notin\mathcal W_b$ for every integer $b\ge2$, and the choice $z_j=(j+S_j)^{-1}$, $\alpha_j=\log_2(1+z_j)$, $c_{j,q_jd}=z_j^{\omega(d)}$ makes the cover cost summable, so $V\in\mathcal C$.

uses.warrant: "The bound is summable in $j$ and already includes the factor $2^{j\alpha_j}$ required by (V), so $V\in\mathcal C$."

steps.label: The gcd-orbit mean (8)
steps.statement: $M_{Q,b}(d):=\lim_{X\to\infty}\frac1X\sum_{m=1}^Xw_{b,d}(Qm)=\frac{g}{d(b^g-1)}\le\frac1d$, where $g=(Q,d)$.

steps.label: Dominated convergence for a fixed modulus
steps.statement: $\frac1X\sum_{m=1}^Xw_{b,d}(Qm)\le\frac{Q+2}{d}$. For this fixed $Q$ the majorant $(Q+2)/d$ is summable over $A$, so dominated convergence takes the limit in the observation length inside the sum over $d$ and gives the Cesàro mean $\sum_{d\in A}M_{Q,b}(d)$.

uses.warrant: The limit taken inside the sum is "the Cesàro mean $\sum_{d\in A}M_{Q,b}(d)$" of (8).

steps.label: The lcm limit (9)
steps.statement: With $Q_t=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,t)$, $\sum_{d\in A}M_{Q_t,b}(d)\longrightarrow X_A(b)$. Hence the limiting displacement means tend to zero.

uses.warrant: "a second dominated-convergence argument, now with the bound $M_{Q_t,b}(d)\le1/d$, yields" (9).

steps.label: Cyclotomic prime-power fact
steps.statement: For a prime $\ell\mid\Phi_n(b)$ and $e=v_\ell(b^n-1)$, $\operatorname{ord}_{\ell^e}(b)=n$ for the full prime power $\ell^e$.

steps.label: The unique-valuation step
steps.locator: Appendix B, after Theorem B.1, p. 16
steps.statement: Fix a divisibility-maximal $n\in F$ with $n\ge2$ and a prime $\ell\mid\Phi_n(b)$. Every other selected exponent $m$ satisfies $n\nmid m$, hence $v_\ell(b^m-1)<e$, so the $n$th summand has the uniquely smallest $\ell$-adic valuation and cannot cancel. Thus $\ell^e\mid D_F$ and $n\mid\operatorname{ord}_{D_F}(b)$.

uses.warrant: "With $e=v_\ell(b^n-1)$, the cyclotomic fact in Section E gives $\operatorname{ord}_{\ell^e}(b)=n$ for the full prime power $\ell^e$."

steps.label: The full support has displacements above 1/2
steps.statement: $\Delta_{2,\mathbb{N}_{>0}}(N)>(2^N-1)\sum_{a>N}2^{-a}=1-2^{-N}\ge\frac12$ $(N\ge1)$. Erdős nevertheless proved the full-support value irrational [erdos1948].

uses.warrant: "Erdős nevertheless proved the full-support value irrational [erdos1948]."

steps.label: The primes have displacements above 1/3
steps.statement: Every prime singleton is admitted by both support criteria, and yet $\Delta_{2,\mathcal P}(N)>1/3$ for every $N\ge1$. Tao and Teräväinen nevertheless prove that $X_{\mathcal P}(2)$ is irrational.

uses.warrant: "Tao and Teräväinen nevertheless prove that $X_{\mathcal P}(2)$ is irrational [taoteravainen2025, Theorem 1.3, p. 4]."

steps.label: The criteria are sufficient, not necessary
steps.statement: All three criteria are sufficient conditions; none of them characterises the supports in Problem 1.1. Small displacement is sufficient for irrationality, and the full support already shows that it is far from necessary.

uses.warrant: "Small displacement is sufficient for irrationality, and the full support already shows that it is far from necessary", followed by the display $\Delta_{2,\mathbb{N}_{>0}}(N)\ge1/2$.
"The set $\mathcal P$ of all primes gives a second obstruction."

steps.label: A rational number has a fixed positive gap
steps.statement: Suppose $S=p/q$. For integers $u,j$, if $uS-j>0$ then $uS-j\ge1/q$; so to prove $S$ irrational we construct integers $u,j$ with $0<uS-j<\frac1q$.

steps.label: The fractional-part formula (2)
steps.statement: $\ell_n(k):=\left\{\frac{2^k-1}{2^n-1}\right\}=\frac{2^{k\bmod n}-1}{2^n-1}$. The fractional part vanishes when $n$ divides $k$ and only then.

steps.label: The split (3) and positive remainders
steps.statement: $(2^k-1)S=J(k)+R(k)$ with $R(k)=\sum_{n\in A}\ell_n(k)$ and $J(k)$ a finite sum of integers. If $A$ is infinite, $S=p/q$ implies $R(k)=(2^k-1)S-J(k)\ge\frac1q$ for every $k\ge1$.

uses.warrant: $R(k)$ is defined as the sum of the fractional parts $\ell_n(k)$ given by (2): "summing these fractional parts will give $R(k)$".
"Therefore $S=p/q\Longrightarrow R(k)=(2^k-1)S-J(k)\ge\frac1q$", the gap of Section 3 applied with $u=2^k-1$, $j=J(k)$.

steps.label: Averaging complete attempts (4)
steps.statement: $\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}R(mQ)=\sum_{n\in A}\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}\ell_n(mQ)$. If this average is below $1/q$, then at least one whole column has total below $1/q$.

steps.label: Complete cycles average below 1/n (5)
steps.statement: Whenever $M$ is a positive multiple of $c=n/\gcd(n,Q)$, $\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}\ell_n(mQ)<\frac1n$.

uses.warrant: The cycle sum is computed from the formula: "each numerator is one less than the corresponding power, so the total over the cycle is" below $1$.

steps.label: A bound for every number of attempts (6)
steps.statement: For every positive $M$, $\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}\ell_n(mQ)\le\frac{2Q}{n}$.

uses.warrant: The consecutive entries are the values $\ell_n(k)$ of (2), which repeat "the block" of $n-1$ increasing positive entries followed by $0$.

steps.label: Explicit cutoffs chosen in the order t, Q, T, M
steps.statement: Choose $t\in A$ with $\sum_{n\in A,\,n>t}1/n<1/(2q)$; a positive common multiple $Q$ of the selected $n\le t$; $T\in A$ with $2Q\sum_{n\in A,\,n>T}1/n<1/(2q)$; and $M$ a positive common multiple of the cycle lengths $n/\gcd(n,Q)$ for $t<n\le T$. Then $\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}R(mQ)<0+\frac1{2q}+\frac1{2q}=\frac1q$.

uses.warrant: "By (4), the average of the column totals is therefore" below $1/q$.
The table's middle row: "complete cycles; row average below $1/n$" for $t<n\le T$.
The table's last row: "bound $2Q/n$ for every $M$" for $n>T$.
